name: Red-White-Red Card (Points-Based Skilled Worker Permit)

qualifying_event.description: A points-based combined work-and-residence permit for third-country nationals, with sub-categories for Very Highly Qualified Workers, Skilled Workers in Shortage Occupations, and Other Key Workers. Applicant must have a concrete job offer and score above the category's minimum points threshold.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Job offer/employment contract; qualification documents; points assessment; employer declaration.

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum 70 of 100 possible points (special qualifications up to 40, work experience up to 20, language skills up to 10, age up to 20, Austrian studies up to 10).
Minimum 55 of 90 (95 with English bonus) points, plus a job offer in an occupation on the annual shortage list; must be paid per the applicable collective bargaining agreement.
Minimum 55 of 90 (95 with English bonus) points, and a gross minimum salary of EUR 3,465/month (2026).
Gross minimum monthly salary of EUR 3,465 (2026) for the Other Key Workers sub-category.

evidence_required.document: Job offer / employment contract (min. 24 months validity)
Passport valid for at least the card's duration

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years, tied to a specific employer

sources.title: migration.gv.at -- Permanent immigration overview: Red-White-Red Card categories (Very Highly Qualified Workers, Skilled Workers in Shortage Occupations, Other Key Workers, etc.)

workinaustria.com (AMS/ABA-run official relocation portal) -- Red-White-Red Card: points thresholds per sub-category, 2026 salary figures, 2-year validity, path to Settlement Permit/Long-Term Resident EU status

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Austria). work_rights modeled 'restricted' since the card is tied to a specific employer/job during its initial 2-year term (full labour-market access only comes with RWR Card Plus or Long-Term Resident EU status -- see at_permanent_residence.json). Salary figures other than the Other Key Workers EUR 3,465/month threshold are pegged to collective bargaining agreements rather than a flat number, so not modeled as a hard numeric requirement for the other two sub-categories. workinaustria.com is Austria's official government-run relocation/labour-market information portal (operated by AMS/ABA), treated as tier-1 alongside migration.gv.at.
